card.title: Vice President of Continuous Improvement & Lean
card.description:
Eaton’s Electrical Sector America’s business is curretly hiring for a VP of Continuous Improvement & Lean. This role can be based at Eaton’s Cleveland or Pittsburgh office. Relocation within hiring country is offered. 50 percent travel is anticipated.

Reporting directly to the SVP of Operations, Electrical Sector – Americas (ESA), the VP of CI & Lean is the senior executive accountable for the vision, strategy, and results of the Eaton Continuous Improvement System (ECIS) across the $16B ESA business, spanning 60 manufacturing sites and 14 divisions. This role sets the multi-year Lean transformation agenda, builds continuous improvement into the sector's strategic and annual profit plans, and holds the business accountable for measurable improvement in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth.

The VP leads and develops the ESA CI team, defines the sector-wide operating model, standards, and governance the team deploys, and serves as a strategic advisor to the ESA leadership team. Rather than leading deployment within a division, this role directs CI resources to the highest-value opportunities, owns the sector's CI talent pipeline, and shapes a Lean leadership culture at the executive level. The VP also represents ESA in enterprise CI forums, partnering with Corporate CI & Quality to align standards and scale best practices across Eaton.

**Job Responsibilities:**
-------------------------

* Defines the multi-year ESA Lean and continuous improvement vision, strategy, and roadmap, and integrates it into the sector's strategic plan and annual profit plan.
* Owns the ECIS operating model for ESA: sets the standards, maturity expectations, and governance that the CI team deploys across divisions, functions, and sites.
* Leads, coaches, and develops the ESA CI team; sets objectives, allocates CI resources, and holds the team accountable for results.
* Chairs the Divisional CI Council across all ESA divisions and leads sector-level performance reviews, establishing the operating cadence that links CI results to business performance.
* Accountable for the ESA cost-out and productivity commitments delivered through CI; builds the sector project pipeline and validates financial impact.
* Serves as strategic advisor to the SVP of Operations and the ESA leadership team, prioritizing the transformation initiatives with the greatest business value.
* Sponsors large-scale, cross-divisional transformations (e.g., footprint changes, acquisition integrations, and Lean in office and transactional processes).
* Builds the sector CI talent strategy: capability standards, certification pathways (e.g., ASCEND X, PME), succession planning, and rotation of high-potential leaders through CI roles.
* Coaches ESA executives on Lean leadership behaviors and role-models a culture of accountability and continuous improvement from the top.
* Sets sector maturity targets and owns the EBSA and OpA assessment strategy; reviews results with leadership and directs closure of systemic gaps.
* Represents ESA in enterprise CI forums; partners with Corporate CI & Quality to shape Eaton-wide standards and scale proven practices across sectors.
* Manages the ESA CI function budget and champions digital and data analytics tools that accelerate improvement.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

Required Qualifications: 

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution.
* Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Quality, or Operations
* Minimum 5 years leading leaders (managers or directors) at a multi-site, division, or business-unit level
* Proven track record leading Lean transformations that delivered measurable financial results, preferably in a multi-division manufacturing environment
* Professional experience in a global matrixed organization
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc

Preferred Qualifications: 

* Master's degree or MBA preferred

Position Success Criteria: 

* Expert-level command of Lean and Six Sigma; Master Black Belt or Black Belt certification required
* Experience designing, governing, and maturing a business operating system and maturity model at scale
* Strong business and financial acumen: builds cost-out and productivity plans, quantifies impact, and ties CI results to the P&L
* Experience designing CI talent, certification, and capability programs across a large, multi-site organization
* Applies Lean to both manufacturing and office/transactional processes
* Executive presence; a trusted advisor who influences, challenges, and aligns senior executives
* Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing teams of senior CI leaders
* Strategic thinker who turns vision into multi-year roadmaps and leads change at scale
* Excellent communication at every level, from the shop floor to the executive leadership team

The expected annual salary range for this role is $203000 - $297000 a year. This position is also eligible for a variable incentive program.

Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.

You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.

We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. Eaton provides various Health and Welfare benefits as well as Retirement benefits, and several programs that provide for paid and unpaid time away from work. Click here for more detail: Eaton Benefits Overview. Please note that specific programs and options available to an employee may depend on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.

**Job Title:** **Senior Manager Manufacturing Training**
========================================================

Req Id: 3772

Work Model: On-Site

Company: Philip Morris USA

State/Province: Virginia

Job Description:

**Together We Innovate. Together We Change.**

 

We are seeking a **Senior Manager, Manufacturing Training** to lead all salaried and hourly training across Cigarette Manufacturing (CM) and Primary, including logistics. This strategic role sets direction, clears roadblocks and owns the budget.

 

**What you will be doing:**

* Own the end-to-end training strategy for salaried, hourly technical and hourly non-technical employees, including the multi-year capability roadmap and annual priorities.
* Anticipate business and technical issues, own the consolidated training demand forecast, and make trade-offs across populations when operations shift.
* Secure leadership commitments across Operations, Engineering, Staffing, OEMs, Finance and the union, and escalate to clear resource roadblocks such as new-equipment training gaps.
* Own the training budget, approve OEM, third-party and travel spend, contract new vendors with Procurement and Legal, and manage the Technician iPad program.
* Own the training logistics standard: master schedule, training calendar and people tracker, equipment and OEM instructor scheduling, LMS records and labor agreement scheduling rules.
* Own the ISO 9001 training quality system and align all training groups to it.
* Set strategy for major initiatives such as North Pole Export, and sponsor training modernization, the innovation strategy and the Manufacturing Knowledge Center.
* Set training-wide objectives, metrics and trainer qualification standard; represent training on the Intergrated Work Systems (IWS) Education & Training Pillar.
 

**What we want you to have:**

* 10+ years in training or manufacturing operations, including leading leaders; Bachelor's required, advanced degree or professional certification preferred.
* In-depth manufacturing process and equipment knowledge, with solutions that span departments.
* Proven ability to set strategy, anticipate business issues and allocate budget.
* Influences across departments; uses candor to challenge others and change direction.
* ISO 9001, LMS and Office 365 experience (Copilot preferred); supports all shifts and works in manufacturing using Personal Protective Equipment (PPE).

**As a People Leader at Altria, you are accountable for both results and the experience of your team. You drive alignment by connecting strategy to daily work, and you model collaboration by embracing diverse perspectives. By creating trust, offering feedback, and leading with authenticity, you help strengthen Altria’s culture and deliver meaningful outcomes.**

 

The starting salary is based on but not limited to experience, knowledge, and qualifications in determining compensation decisions. The Salary Range for this position is: $132,500.00 - $202,100.00.

 

**Why You’ll Love Building Your Career at Altria**

 

At Altria, we believe a great career starts with feeling supported — both at work and in life. Here’s what you’ll find here:

* **Own your time** — start with 15 days of paid time off, 13 paid holidays, and a 37.5-hour workweek so you can recharge and live fully.
* **A place where you belong** — where your ideas are welcomed, your growth is encouraged, and your impact is real.
* **Get recognized for your work** — annual merit increases and performance bonus.
* **A future you can count on** — 401(k) matching from day one; plus Deferred Profit Sharing, an annual company contribution in an amount equal to 13%–17% of your base salary.
* **Help with your goals** — get help with student loan repayment assistance, attend a conference, or gain a new certification with professional development stipends.
* **Support for what matters most** — comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family.
* **Celebrating your milestones** — paid parental and bonding leave for life’s biggest moments.
* **Wellness that goes beyond work** — programs that care for your whole well-being at whatever stage you are in your life.
* **A culture that gives back** — paid volunteer days and a shared commitment to making a difference.
 

**At Altria, we offer more than benefits — we offer a career that fits your life, rewards your ambition, and celebrates your impact.**

 

This position is not eligible for sponsorship.

**Altria is a Fortune 500 company that has a leading portfolio of products for U.S. adult tobacco and nicotine consumers 21+. For decades we’ve been leaders in the tobacco industry, but the industry is evolving - and so are we. Our Vision is Moving Beyond Smoking™.**

**At Altria, we celebrate the power of diverse teams working together to shape our future. Each Altria company is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing individuals with criminal records, including formerly incarcerated individuals and individuals with conviction records, a fair chance at employment. Join us as we work together to shape a better future for adult tobacco consumers, our employees, and our shareholders.**

**Altria is the parent company of Philip Morris USA, John Middleton, U.S. Smokeless Tobacco, Helix Innovations, and NJOY. Altria complements its tobacco portfolio with equity investments in Anheuser-Busch InBev and Cronos Group.**

card.description:
**PLANT OPERATIONS CAREERS**

Plant Manager

Lead a healthcare laundry plant.

**Where** [City, ST]

**Reports to** General Manager / Regional Vice President

As Plant Manager, you'll lead the full plant (production, maintenance, quality, and logistics) with accountability for safety, budget, and the healthcare customers who depend on clean, safe linen every day.

Why you'll like it here

**Own the plant**

Daily operations, people, budget, and results.

**Lean in action**

Drive improvement with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.

**Lead leaders**

Develop supervisors, maintenance staff, and production Associates.

**Healthcare standards**

Run an operation held to OSHA and HLAC requirements.

What you'll own

* Lead and manage the Safety & Health Program within the production environment.
* Lead, motivate, and develop a team of supervisors, maintenance staff, and production associates.
* Oversee daily plant operations, including production scheduling, labor forecasting, staffing, and workflow optimization.
* Drive process improvements using Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Manage plant budget, including labor, maintenance, and operational expenses.
* Oversee inventory management to ensure consistent material supply and stock levels.

What you need

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, or Business Administration required.
* 5–7 years of leadership experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
* Strong end-to-end understanding of plant operations, including safety, quality, maintenance, and compliance.
* Proven experience managing P&L, budgeting, payroll, and cost controls.
* Strong problem-solving, analytical, and strategic thinking skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and ERP systems.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills.

**Physical requirements**

* Ability to stand, walk, and move throughout a manufacturing facility for extended periods.
* Ability to occasionally lift up-to fifty (50) pounds.
* Comfortable working in a plant/production environment.
* Ability to push and pull carts of linen regularly.
* Ability to use required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, and work boots.

**Bonus points**

* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Six Sigma methodologies preferred.
* PMP (Project Management Professional) certification.
* Willing to relocate- GOE flexibility.
* Prior military leadership experience (e.g., Sergeant or above) a plus.
* Familiarity with ISO 14001 / ISO 9001 and GMP standards.
* Experience with manufacturing systems and reporting tools

**We'll teach you:** Our plant network, operating standards, and the support of a national organization.

How we work

Every ImageFIRST Associate lives our four Core Values. These are our required competencies.

**Be Respectful**

Value all we come in contact with.

**Be Remarkable**

Create a positive moment with every interaction.

**Be Safe**

Keep ourselves and those around us safe.

**Be Honest**

Be guided by truthfulness in all we do.

Great work gets noticed

**Everyday recognition**

Coworkers nominate each other for going above and beyond, and those nominations go up in the office for everyone to see.

**All Stars & Council of Excellence**

Each year, Associates who live our values are nominated as All-Stars and earn a certificate and a cash award. Top winners join the Council of Excellence with an additional reward.

Benefits

Weekly pay

Medical, Dental, Vision

Pet, Legal, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance

401(k) with company match

Paid Time Off package

Paid Parental Leave

Tuition Reimbursement

Referral Program

Great company culture

Collaborative team environment

 

**MILITARY & VETERANS**

Served? Your skills fit here.

Officers and senior NCOs who led maintenance, logistics, or production operations: command a plant. Whether you're transitioning out, serving in the Guard or Reserve, or a veteran, we want to hear from you.

* Leading a unit leading supervisors, maintenance, and production
* Readiness and inspections safety, quality, and compliance
* Resource stewardship plant budget and cost control

Guard and Reserve members: we support your service commitments. Tell us your branch and specialty when you apply.

 

Who we are

ImageFIRST is the nation's largest medical-focused linen and laundry provider, serving health systems, hospitals, and outpatient facilities since 1967. We run more HLAC-accredited facilities than anyone else, and 97% of our customers stay with us.

Our mission: improving the lives of our associates, our customers, and the patients they serve.

**If you're ready to own a plant's results, apply today.**

 

**Equal Opportunity Employer / Drug-Free Workplace**

We maintain a drug-free workplace in compliance with state and federal law. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are fueled by the talent, passion, and diversity of our associates.

card.title: Director, MSAT/External Manufacturing Management
card.description:
OPPORTUNITY

Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).

All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.

This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Process scale-up and technology transfer

* Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
* Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
* Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
* Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities

Process characterization and PPQ readiness

* Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
* Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
* Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification

**Company Description**

AZZ Inc. is a leading provider of specialized products and services designed to meet the unique needs of industrial markets worldwide. With a rich history spanning several decades, AZZ has established a strong reputation for innovation, quality, and customer satisfaction.

At AZZ, our culture is defined by **trust**, **respect**, **accountability**, **integrity**, **teamwork** and **safety** ("TRAITS"). We are dedicated to our employees by fully training and equipping them and providing a safe environment to grow personally and professionally. We strive to build, maintain and create a work environment that attracts and retains employees who are high contributors, have outstanding skills, are engaged in our culture, and who embody our Company mission: to create superior value in a culture where people can grow both professionally and personally, and where TRAITS matter.

As AZZ Inc. continues to evolve and innovate, it remains committed to driving shareholder value while maintaining its reputation as a leader in industrial solutions. With a strong foundation built on decades of experience and a forward-thinking approach, AZZ Inc. is poised to continue its upward trajectory, delivering sustainable growth and an unwavering commitment to excellence.

 **Job Description**

AZZ has an opportunity for a Plant Manager at our Canton facility. Reporting to the Regional Director of Operations, this role is responsible for, but not limited to, directing and managing all plant operations with overall responsibility for production, maintenance, quality, and personnel. You are a strong leader with a track record of effectively managing, mentoring, and developing leaders. You are experienced in developing and implementing business strategies and can deliver outstanding service to both internal and external stakeholders.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Directs and manages plant operations for production, maintenance, quality, shipping and receiving and all personnel activities.
* Develops and controls profits/loss, business plans and budget restrictions.
* Implements cost effective systems for control over capital, operating expenditures, manpower, wages, and salaries.
* Establishes and monitors overall plant performance for production and quality standards while maintaining strict process controls.
* Maintains existing plant facilities and equipment. Replaces or adjusts plant facilities and equipment when necessary.
* Provides leadership and training to accomplish the company goals and objectives.
* Implements and maintains preventative maintenance programs.
* Maintains and enforces OSHA and other safety regulations.
* Recommends or implements measures to motivate employees and to improve production methods, equipment performance, product quality or efficiency.
* Recommends personnel action including, but not limited to, annual evaluations, promotions, hiring and firing.
* Responsible for maintaining high levels of customer satisfaction.
* Serves as the primary direct report for all facility personnel.

 
**Qualifications** 

* 3 – 5 years of management experience **required**
* Experience in steel fabrication, metal coatings, or hot dip galvanizing **required**
* Proficient in all Microsoft Office applications, i.e., Excel, Outlook, and Word
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Ability to effectively handle and manage confidential and sensitive information
* Knowledge of safety and OSHA rules and regulations required
* Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and SOPs for heavy industrial equipment

**Minimum Education**

* Bachelor’s Degree required

 
**Additional Information**

**What We Offer**

* Competitive salary and bonus structure.
* Comprehensive health, dental, and vision benefits package.
* Retirement savings plan with company match.
* Opportunities for professional growth and development in a dynamic industry.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

#LI-Onsite

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer.

AZZ Inc. is a Drug Free Workplace

card.description:
**Position Summary**
====================

Oversee the assigned plant’s operations and maintenance delivered by the third-party operations and maintenance contractor (the Contractor) and take Company-level responsibility for safe, reliable, efficient and cost-effective power generation. Protect equipment condition and monitor delivery against agreed production, availability and contractual targets. Oversee plant resources, costs, records and stakeholder interfaces from commissioning and operational handover through ongoing operation.

The Contractor retains day-to-day operational control, provides the workforce and executes routine plant activities under the agreed contract. The Plant Manager is responsible for ensuring that the Contractor delivers plant results in line with the contract, overseeing its performance, giving technical and operational instructions to its site management as the contract allows, deciding the critical matters, and intervening when safety, performance, equipment integrity or delivery is at risk.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

* Lead plant readiness for commissioning and operational handover with Projects, Technical, HSE and the Contractor, ensuring personnel, training, procedures, spares, maintenance systems and emergency plans are ready.
* Drive closure of handover gaps and punch-list items before and after operational handover.
* Review and approve production and operating plans prepared with the Contractor, considering demand forecasts, available capacity, equipment limits and project commitments.
* Monitor generation, availability, reliability, capacity factor, heat rate, fuel and auxiliary consumption and forced-outage performance against targets; require corrective and improvement actions from the Contractor and verify they achieve the intended results.
* Oversee heat rate improvement and auxiliary consumption reduction initiatives with the Contractor and Technical teams, and obtain approval for proposed modifications under the change management procedure.
* Review the effect of startup/shutdown cycles and load-following operation on equipment life, thermal fatigue and availability, and agree operating and maintenance strategies with the Contractor and OEMs accordingly.
* Hold daily operating coordination and plant performance reviews with the Contractor’s management, resolve operational conflicts and maintain plant risk and action registers.
* Review and approve preventive, predictive and corrective maintenance plans, overhaul scopes and outage schedules prepared with the Contractor, taking account of OEM guidance, asset condition, warranty terms, production commitments and approved budgets.
* Oversee gas and steam turbine lifecycle management with the Contractor and OEMs, including tracking of life-limited parts, rotor and stator life and fatigue effects, and integrate it into maintenance and capital planning.
* Oversee maintenance and repair execution for work quality, timely completion and minimum disruption to generation; require recovery plans or changes to resources or work methods when delivery is at risk.
* Lead the response to major equipment failures with the Contractor’s specialists, Company engineers and OEMs: approve containment and recovery actions, ensure root cause analysis is completed and authorize safe return to service.
* Oversee the Contractor’s management of spare parts, consumables, chemicals and lubricants; set critical stock priorities, resolve shortages, review technical specifications of purchase requests and ensure technical acceptance, proper storage and effective inventory control.
* Manage plant interfaces with Technical teams for utilities and shared equipment under the agreed responsibility split, and ensure assigned statutory inspections are completed with the responsible functions.
* Administer the plant O&M contract and hold the Contractor to its agreed scope, staffing coverage, service levels and technical obligations; address nonperformance with its management and require recovery plans within contractual authority.
* Prepare formal notices and claim inputs with relevant functions.
* Oversee warranty and warranty claim processes and technical disputes with OEMs and suppliers, including long-term service agreement matters, and manage technical communication with them.
* Verify the Contractor’s invoices, labor hours, overtime, reimbursable costs, materials and subcontractor charges against contract rates, authorized work and actual delivery; challenge unsupported charges and recommend verified services for approval through the Company’s payment approval workflow.
* Prepare the plant O&M budget and forecasts, control commitments and expenditure against the approved budget and act on variances.
* Evaluate additional work requests, maintain change and claim records and obtain O&M Director approval for decisions beyond approved budget or contractual authority.
* Ensure accurate production, fuel-consumption and customer and revenue meter records and timely plant reporting; provide validated data and technical explanations to Commercial and Finance for customer billing and contractual reconciliations.
* Identify gaps in O&M service capability and recommend alternative O&M contractors or specialist support to the O&M Director; contribute to technical scopes, contractor sourcing and proposal evaluation, and manage site transition and handover to preserve operating continuity when the Contractor changes.
* Oversee plant HSE requirements with HSE and the Contractor’s management, including work permits, energy isolation, waste controls and emergency preparedness; stop unsafe work and direct immediate containment and incident response under site procedures.
* Ensure plans are in place for high-risk process safety scenarios (gas or steam turbine trips, HRSG pressure events, plant blackout) and lead the response in a crisis.
* Promote a safety culture through visible leadership, participation in safety activities and training, and ensure that work is carried out with safety as an integral part of the job.
* Ensure compliance with applicable environmental permits, emission limits and monitoring and reporting requirements, in coordination with HSE and Permitting.
* Lead plant coordination with customers, grid operators and other stakeholders under agreed communication protocols, including dispatch communication and contractual availability and performance obligations.
* Ensure the plant meets grid operator and off-taker requirements for frequency, voltage, reactive power and load-change capability.
* Lead inspection and audit preparation and ensure responsible parties complete corrective actions, records and required submissions.
* Review the Contractor’s staffing and shift plans against contract requirements, require adequate competence and coverage and resolve staffing deficiencies through its management. Recruitment, payroll and employment administration remain with the Contractor.
* Ensure accurate operating, maintenance and equipment records and timely daily, weekly and monthly performance reports, including capacity utilization analysis, to the O&M Director.
* Ensure plant administrative, operating and maintenance procedures and documentation are established and aligned with applicable safety, environmental and quality management system requirements, and follow the Company’s risk management approach.
* Contribute to short, medium and long-term plant strategy, including reliability and capital investment planning, with the O&M Director.

**Required Qualifications**
===========================

* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical, Electronics, Energy Systems, Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline preferred.
* Minimum 10 years of power generation O&M experience in natural gas-fired combined cycle plants, with responsibility for plant operations, maintenance and technical team leadership.
* Hands-on knowledge of combined cycle systems, including heavy-duty gas turbines, HRSGs, steam turbines, generators, water and steam chemistry, balance-of-plant equipment and DCS controls, with the ability to lead complex troubleshooting.
* Prior Plant Manager, Operations Manager or Maintenance Manager experience at a combined cycle plant.
* Experience with the gas turbine technology installed at the assigned plant (for example Siemens Energy or GE frame units).
* Experience planning and managing major outages and inspections (combustion, hot gas path, major overhaul) with OEMs and multiple contractors.
* Experience overseeing an outsourced O&M contractor or equivalent contract oversight, including performance management, labor-hour and invoice control, budgets and reporting.
* Experience with OEM long-term service agreements and warranty management.
* US operating experience, including independent power producers or owner-side operations.
* Working knowledge of NERC reliability requirements as applicable, environmental permit and emissions compliance, lockout/tagout and permit-to-work systems, and EHS regulations.
* Understanding of power market operations, including dispatch, availability obligations and commercial reporting to customers.
* Competence in CMMS and reporting tools; fluent English and MS Office proficiency.
* Training or certification in combined cycle O&M, leadership and team management, and problem-solving and decision-making techniques is preferred.
* Authorization to work in the United States. Ability to work at the assigned US site, travel as required.

Eaton’s Electrical Sector America’s business is curretly hiring for a VP of Continuous Improvement & Lean. This role can be based at Eaton’s Cleveland or Pittsburgh office. Relocation within hiring country is offered. 50 percent travel is anticipated.
 
 
Reporting directly to the SVP of Operations, Electrical Sector – Americas (ESA), the VP of CI & Lean is the senior executive accountable for the vision, strategy, and results of the Eaton Continuous Improvement System (ECIS) across the $16B ESA business, spanning 60 manufacturing sites and 14 divisions. This role sets the multi-year Lean transformation agenda, builds continuous improvement into the sector's strategic and annual profit plans, and holds the business accountable for measurable improvement in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth.
 
 
The VP leads and develops the ESA CI team, defines the sector-wide operating model, standards, and governance the team deploys, and serves as a strategic advisor to the ESA leadership team. Rather than leading deployment within a division, this role directs CI resources to the highest-value opportunities, owns the sector's CI talent pipeline, and shapes a Lean leadership culture at the executive level. The VP also represents ESA in enterprise CI forums, partnering with Corporate CI & Quality to align standards and scale best practices across Eaton.
 
 
**Job Responsibilities**

* Defines the multi-year ESA Lean and continuous improvement vision, strategy, and roadmap, and integrates it into the sector's strategic plan and annual profit plan.
* Owns the ECIS operating model for ESA: sets the standards, maturity expectations, and governance that the CI team deploys across divisions, functions, and sites.
* Leads, coaches, and develops the ESA CI team; sets objectives, allocates CI resources, and holds the team accountable for results.
* Chairs the Divisional CI Council across all ESA divisions and leads sector-level performance reviews, establishing the operating cadence that links CI results to business performance.
* Accountable for the ESA cost-out and productivity commitments delivered through CI; builds the sector project pipeline and validates financial impact.
* Serves as strategic advisor to the SVP of Operations and the ESA leadership team, prioritizing the transformation initiatives with the greatest business value.
* Sponsors large-scale, cross-divisional transformations (e.g., footprint changes, acquisition integrations, and Lean in office and transactional processes).
* Builds the sector CI talent strategy: capability standards, certification pathways (e.g., ASCEND X, PME), succession planning, and rotation of high-potential leaders through CI roles.
* Coaches ESA executives on Lean leadership behaviors and role-models a culture of accountability and continuous improvement from the top.
* Sets sector maturity targets and owns the EBSA and OpA assessment strategy; reviews results with leadership and directs closure of systemic gaps.
* Represents ESA in enterprise CI forums; partners with Corporate CI & Quality to shape Eaton-wide standards and scale proven practices across sectors.
* Manages the ESA CI function budget and champions digital and data analytics tools that accelerate improvement.

**Qualifications**
Required Qualifications:
 
 

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution.
* Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Quality, or Operations
* Minimum 5 years leading leaders (managers or directors) at a multi-site, division, or business-unit level
* Proven track record leading Lean transformations that delivered measurable financial results, preferably in a multi-division manufacturing environment
* Professional experience in a global matrixed organization
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree or MBA preferred

**Position Success Criteria**

* Expert-level command of Lean and Six Sigma; Master Black Belt or Black Belt certification required
* Experience designing, governing, and maturing a business operating system and maturity model at scale
* Strong business and financial acumen: builds cost-out and productivity plans, quantifies impact, and ties CI results to the P&L
* Experience designing CI talent, certification, and capability programs across a large, multi-site organization
* Applies Lean to both manufacturing and office/transactional processes
* Executive presence; a trusted advisor who influences, challenges, and aligns senior executives
* Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing teams of senior CI leaders
* Strategic thinker who turns vision into multi-year roadmaps and leads change at scale
* Excellent communication at every level, from the shop floor to the executive leadership team

The expected annual salary range for this role is $203000 - $297000 a year. This position is also eligible for a variable incentive program.
 
 
Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.
 
 
All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.
 
 
We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.
 
 
Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.
 
 
You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.
 
 
To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.

card.description:
At UVeye, we're on a mission to redefine vehicle safety and reliability on a global scale. Founded in 2016, we pioneered the world's first fully automated suite of AI-powered vehicle inspection systems, combining computer vision, machine learning, and generative AI.

With over $380M in funding and strategic partnerships with Toyota, Amazon, General Motors, JLR, Volvo, and Hertz, our technology is deployed across manufacturing plants, dealerships, wholesale auctions, fleets, and seaports worldwide. Named one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies of 2026, our 270+ global employees are solutions-oriented, accountable, and driven by one shared goal: making roads safer for everyone.

We are seeking an experienced Vice President, Global Supply Chain to lead the strategy and execution of our end-to-end global supply chain, including procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier management, inventory planning, logistics, and warehouse operations. This executive will build scalable capabilities that support company growth, successful installations, and reliable field service across multiple geographies, with accountability for delivery performance, cost, working capital, and supply continuity.

This role requires a strategic, hands-on leader who can set long-term direction while working directly with teams and suppliers to negotiate critical agreements, resolve material constraints, and improve operational performance. Partnering closely with the COO and executive leadership team, the VP will align supply chain priorities with business objectives, strengthen planning and operational visibility, and develop a high-performing organization with clear ownership and measurable results.

A day in the life and how you’ll make an impact:

* Set the global supply chain strategy. Develop and execute a multiyear roadmap aligned with growth plans, installation requirements, service commitments, and financial objectives.
* Own operational and financial performance. Establish accountability for total supply chain cost, inventory investment, delivery reliability, and warehouse productivity. Partner with Finance to develop budgets, evaluate investments, and deliver measurable improvements.
* Connect business demand with supply execution. Establish a cross-functional planning cadence that aligns forecasts, installation schedules, field service requirements, supplier capacity, and inventory availability. Surface constraints early and drive decisions that protect customer commitments.
* Lead strategic sourcing and supplier performance. Develop sourcing strategies, negotiate commercial agreements, and build supplier relationships that improve cost, quality, lead times, and capacity. Hold suppliers accountable through clear expectations and performance reviews.
* Build supply resilience. Identify critical dependencies and develop mitigation plans for supplier disruption, capacity constraints, long lead times, and cross-border risks.
* Optimize inventory and material availability. Establish inventory policies that balance installation and service readiness with working capital discipline, reducing shortages, excess stock, and obsolescence.
* Direct global logistics and warehouse operations. Design scalable distribution capabilities and oversee freight, import/export, fulfillment, and material flow to installation sites and field teams. Ensure safe, accurate, compliant, and efficient operations.
* Strengthen systems, data, and decision-making. Set standards for ERP data integrity, inventory visibility, and reporting. Prioritize improvements in systems and automation that support scale and better operational decisions.
* Build and develop the organization. Define the team structure, hire and develop strong leaders, establish succession plans, and create a culture of ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

card.title: Sr. Director, Quality Operations
card.description:
**The Asahi Kasei Group operates with a commitment of creating for tomorrow. Our business sectors,** ***Materials, Homes, and Health Care*** **, contribute to the development of society by anticipating the changing needs of those around the world. We look for candidates that offer a fresh perspective and a variety of skills to help us achieve our commitment.**
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 
 
Asahi Kasei Therapeutics is the global specialty pharmaceutical business of Asahi Kasei. We are a commercial-stage company committed to positively impacting health by expanding therapeutic options that improve the lives of patients around the world. Drawing upon our strong heritage of scientific innovation, we aim to help reshape care in transplantation, nephrology, immunology, infectious diseases and other underserved conditions. 
 

**Job Description:**

 

The Senior Director of Quality Operations is a strategic and hands‑on leader responsible for ensuring the quality and compliance of all GMP/GDP activities executed internally and by external partners for the company’s products, supporting both clinical trials and commercial distribution, working with the VP of QA, QC and AD

 

This role provides oversight across CDMOs and testing labs, ensuring timely product disposition, investigation management, and quality support throughout the product lifecycle.

 

The base compensation range for this role is $230-260K. Base Compensation is influenced by many factors including, but not limited to: time in the role, previous experience, skills, knowledge, performance, work requirements, internal equity, and business / economic conditions.

 

The Senior Director QA Operations is accountable and responsible to:

* Ensure that the company's global Quality Management System (QMS), processes, and procedures required in the development, manufacture, supply and distribution and related activities are established, maintained and continuously improved in compliance with applicable laws and regulations, including but not necessarily limited to GMP and GDP.
* Provide global and independent Quality Management support, and in particular GMP and GDP oversight, leadership, expertise, reviews and as required quality approvals.
* Assure a satisfactory state of control and compliance with the AKTX QMS, and applicable GMP and GDP standards, authorizations, internal policies, procedures and protocols related to product for clinical trials and commercial manufacturing,
* Actively identify and communicate compliance issues or risks, develop and oversee plans to rectify issues or mitigate risks.

The Senior QA Director works in close collaboration with AKTX functional heads and process owners leading the development, supply and distribution of AKTX medicinal products.

 

**Tasks and responsibilities/accountabilities**

* Take an active role in development and delivery of AKTX strategy, objectives and targets.
* Support development of the QA unit and its way of working, budget, and deliverables in accordance with agreed corporate and individual objectives.
* Lead QA Operations and provide strategic leadership to QA operations staff by driving development, performance, coaching initiatives and ensuring optimal resource allocation to achieve organizational goals and deliver on targets, and objectives
* Collaborate within QA and with process owners, management and departments to establish, maintain and continually improve a fit-for-purpose, robust and effective global QMS.
* Act as owner of assigned business and quality management processes within the QMS and drive and ensure their suitability and effectiveness, and continual improvements.
* Provide oversight across CDMOs and service providers for clinical and commercial programs, ensuring timely product disposition, investigation management, and quality support throughout the product lifecycle.
* Serve as the quality lead in cross-functional CMC teams, partnering with MTO, QC/AD, Regulatory, Clinical, PAM and Supply Chain to ensure end-to-end GMP compliance
* Represent QA in governance and escalation forums for manufacturing investigations, supplier issues, or product quality events
* Own and continuously improve core quality systems including batch release, deviation/CAPA and change control and ensure scalability.
* Provide Quality Oversight, and support of:
 + Suppliers and other third parties involved in outsourced activities or procured material and services to AKTX, including development and follow up of quality and service agreements.
 + Assigned projects related to product and process development, supply and distribution of medicinal products.
 + Assigned computerized systems and other infrastructure within AKTX group.
* Support, and as agreed lead,
 + the management/coordination of regulatory inspections and audits by partners, related to AKTX QMS, and GMP and GDP activities.
 + inspection readiness and QA support during audits and health authority inspections at CDMOs
 + internal audits and audits of engaged suppliers and vendors for outsourced activities and of procured services, including planning, and delivery of the audit program.
 + investigations related to product complaints, issues, deviations, and other findings to identify root causes, corrections, risk mitigations, corrective or preventive actions in collaboration with related experts within the field.
* Support, as applicable, writing, review and approval of governing documentation such as protocols, applications and regulatory files related to Quality Management, and in particular GMP and GDP.
* Lead by example through ensuring own compliance with AKTX policies, values and procedures as well as promoting own team and wider AKTX to do so.
Maintain a contemporary knowledge of current industry trends, standards and methodologies within the area 

 

**Delegations**

* Authority to execute management approvals (or rejection) of governing, controlling and compliance documents and records, such as but not limited to procedures, protocols, reports, statements and methods, for processes owned by the QA unit and managed within AKTX QMS.
* Authority to execute quality and compliance (QA) approvals, consent or rejections of batches of medicinal products for use in clinical studies or intended for commercial distribution.
* Authority to execute quality and compliance (QA) approvals, consent or rejections of proposed changes, investigations of product complaints, deviations, or issues, and resulting corrections or corrective and preventive actions, related to supply, product or process development of medicinal products.
On behalf of AKTX, authority to approve Quality Agreements, including associated schedules, amendments and equivalent, with engaged suppliers, service providers, license partners and other third parties. 

 

**Competence requirements for the position (education and experience)**

* Bachelor's or Master's Degree in relevant applied sciences, e.g. pharmacy, medicine, chemistry, biology and/or engineering (pharmaceutical, chemical or biotechnology).
At least 10 years working experience in quality management, assurance or control, supply chain, regulatory affairs and/or product or process development of medicinal products or other life-science related industry (e.g. medical devices). 

 

#LI-AS1 #Hybrid

 

*As an equal opportunity employer, Asahi Kasei believes a diverse workforce will provide us with the ability to continuously support the changes in the economy, society, and environment.*

card.description:
Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. At KinderCare Learning Companies, the first and only early childhood education provider recognized with the**Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award**, we offer a variety of early education and child care options for families. Whether it’s KinderCare Learning Centers, Champions, or Crème de la Crème, we build confidence for kids, families, and the future we share. And we want you to join us in shaping it—in neighborhoods, at work, and in schools nationwide.

At Crème de la Crème, learning comes alive like nowhere else. Our centers are places that never stand still because kids never do. And when you join us, you’ll become part of that magic—making a memorable impact on young learners and their families every day. In our wow-worthy world of learning, your talents will be the catalyst for creating child care experiences you've never imagined. You’ll link arms with other exceptional humans who care as much about helping kids reach their highest potential as you do—and you’ll know that your work matters.

* As the Crème School Director of Education and Quality, you will 
 + Lead and develop teachers to ensure curriculum alignment with best practices, state standards, and the individual needs of children.
 + Facilitate training and implementation of our comprehensive and developmentally appropriate curriculum for early childhood education.
 + Provide transformative leadership in the field of early childhood education, staying informed about current trends, research, and best practices.
 + Develop a culture of continuous learning and professional development while leading the teaching staff.
 + Establish and maintain high-quality standards for early childhood education program
 + Conduct regular assessments, evaluations, and audits to ensure compliance with Crème standards and licensing requirements
 + Provide guidance and support to teaching staff, promoting a positive and collaborative work environment. In partnership with the Executive Director, host professional development programs to enhance educators' skills and knowledge.
 + Cultivate positive relationships with teachers and parents, involving them in their child's education and development.
 + Collaborate with the community to enhance the educational experience and promote your school within the community.
 + Assist as needed in daily school operations, at times including direct supervision of children
 + Apply data-driven insights to assess program effectiveness, implement strategies to address identified areas of improvement, fostering a culture of continuous quality enhancement.
* Qualifications:
* + Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, Education Administration, or a related field. (preferred)
 + Meet state specific credentials / guidelines for the role
 + At least one year leadership experience in early childhood education or a related field
 + Proven understanding of early childhood development, educational best practices, and program administration.
 + Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
 + Outstanding customer service skills, strong organizational skills, and multi-task and handle multiple situations optimally.
 + Proven ability to build and sustain positive relationships with diverse staff, families, and community. Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in education.
 + Physically able to use a computer with basic proficiency, lift a minimum of 40pounds, and work indoors or outdoors.
 + Able to assume postures in low levels to allow physical and visual contact with children, see and hear well enough to keep children safe, and engage in physical activity.
 + Read, write, understand, and speak English to connect with children and their parents in English.

Range of pay $34,216.00 - $62,100.00 Salary

**Our benefits meet you where you are.** We’re here to help our employees navigate the integration of work and life: 

* Know your whole family is supported with **discounted child care** benefits.

* Breathe easy with **medical, dental, and vision** benefits for your family (and pets, too!).
* Feel supported in your mental health and personal growth with **employee assistance programs.**
* Feel great and thrive with access to **health and wellness programs, paid time off** and **discounts** for work necessities, such as cell phones.
* … and much more.

 
.

We operate research-backed, accredited, and customizable programs in more than 2,000 sites and centers across 40 states and the District of Columbia. As we expand, we’re matching the needs of more and more families, dynamic work environments, and diverse communities from coast to coast. Because we believe every family deserves access to high-quality child care, no matter who they are or where they live. Every day, you’ll help bring this mission to life by building community and delivering exceptional experiences. And if you’re anything like us, you’ll come for the work, and stay for the people.

*KinderCare Learning Companies is an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, age, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, gender identity or expression, or any other basis protected by local, state, or federal law.*

Director, Quality Assurance - Homebased - Blue Bell and Rochester 
 

ICON is a global healthcare intelligence and clinical research organisation united by a mission to bring new medicines and treatments to patients faster.

 
 

As a values-driven organisation, integrity, collaboration, agility, and inclusion are at the heart of how we work and interact with each other, customers, patients and suppliers.

 
 

As a Director, Quality Assurance at ICON, you will ensure the quality and compliance of clinical trials, interpret regulatory requirements, and contribute to the advancement of innovative treatments and therapies.

 

**What You Will Do:**

Your focus will be on driving quality assurance and compliance performance, ensuring quality, and building capability across your area (specifically Imaging and Cardiac Services).
 
 
Key responsibilities include:

 

* Serving as the QA business partner to Medical Imaging and Cardiac Services leadership and teams, providing strategic guidance on quality, regulatory compliance, and emerging risk.
* Leading the development and implementation of quality assurance strategies and processes to support clinical trial activities including establishing quality priorities with leadership and integrating quality considerations into business and operational planning.
* Conducting comprehensive quality assessments and audits to ensure compliance with regulatory standards and guidelines.
* Collaborating with cross-functional teams to identify and address quality issues and implement corrective actions as needed; analyzing quality trends to identify systemic risk and preventive improvement opportunities
* Providing expert guidance and support to staff regarding quality assurance policies, procedures, and best practices.
* Contributing to the continuous improvement of quality management systems and documentation. Promote a proactive culture of quality and continuous improvement.
* Establish quality priorities with IMC leadership and integrate quality considerations into business and operational planning.
* Provide strategic oversight of the risk-based IMC audit program, including internal and vendor audits.
* Represent Quality & Compliance in strategic sponsor relationships, governance, and significant quality escalations. Support the development, interpretation, and governance of quality agreements.
 

**Your Profile:**

You will bring significant quality assurance and compliance experience, with a track record of building high-performing teams and delivering results.
 
 
Required qualifications and experience:

* Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, or related field; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in quality assurance within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, Medical Imaging or CRO industry, with significant experience in a leadership role.
* Extensive knowledge of regulatory requirements and guidelines governing clinical trials (e.g., ICH-GCP, FDA regulations). Knowledge of AI governance and regulations is advantageous.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify and resolve complex quality issues.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and stakeholders.
* Strong leadership skills including cross functional management
* Willingness to travel as required (approximately 25%)

* Competitive base salary and performance related incentives
* Health and wellbeing programmes including medical, dental, and vision coverage where applicable
* Retirement and pension plans
* Life assurance and disability coverage
* Employee assistance programmes and wellbeing resources
* Learning and development opportunities through structured training and career pathways
 

 

Benefits may vary depending on role and location.

* Experience leading performance/load testing (e.g., JMeter, k6, Gatling, LoadRunner) and partnering on security testing practices.
* Strong working knowledge of Agile/Scrum methodologies, the SDLC, and defect management tools (e.g., Jira, TestRail, Zephyr, Xray).
* Demonstrated ability to define, track, and report QA metrics and KPIs to drive continuous improvement.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with both technical and business audiences.

### **Preferred**

* Experience in fintech, payments, banking, or other regulated financial services environments.
* Working awareness of PCI-DSS, SOC 2 Type II, and related compliance requirements as they apply to testing, test data, and change management.
* Experience testing cloud-native and distributed architectures (AWS preferred), microservices, and high-volume transaction systems.
* Experience managing offshore, nearshore, or outsourced QA partners.
* Proficiency in one or more programming languages (e.g., Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, C#) used for test automation.
* Certifications such as ISTQB Advanced/Expert Level, CSTE, or Certified Scrum Master (CSM).

We believe that performance and experience go hand in hand - *an exceptional employee experience is earned through contribution*. We are a results-driven team, grounded in our core values: ownership, authenticity, service, trust, innovation, and camaraderie.

Our culture is built for those who want to make an impact. We challenge each other to grow, celebrate progress, and support one another through shared goals and real connection. Whether you're building technology, serving clients, or supporting internal teams, you’ll be part of a company that empowers you to perform at your best and be known for results.

**Compensation range:** $233K-$291K USD, $190K-$257K CAD 
We invest in the whole employee - personally and professionally. Our benefits package is designed to support your well-being, growth, and success - both inside and outside of work.

**Financial Wellness**

* HSA and FSA options
* Financial wellness resources and employee discount programs

**Health & Well-being**

* Medical, dental, and vision coverage
* Mental health support for employees and dependents through Lyra Health
* Family planning and women’s health benefits through Carrot
* Gym membership reimbursement and virtual wellness programs (including yoga)

**Time Off**

* 3 weeks PTO to start, with unlimited PTO after year one

**Growth & Development**

* Education expense reimbursement
* Leadership development programs
* Certified Payments Professional (CPP) certification support

We believe great performance starts with feeling supported - and we’ve built our benefits with that in mind.

**Traditional Physical Requirements:**

* Requires prolonged sitting, standing, bending, stooping and stretching.
* Requires the ability to lift 10 pounds.
* Requires eye-hand coordination, manual dexterity and a normal range of hearing and vision (with or without correction).

Join our team at Priority Commerce and be part of a dynamic and innovative company that is transforming the financial technology landscape. Together, we can shape the future of payments and banking solutions while providing unmatched value to our clients.

card.description:
**CREATE is growing, and we’re looking for an experienced architect to help us raise the bar.** We’re looking for a licensed architect with 15+ years of experience who loves both sides of architecture: creating great design and figuring out how to actually build it. This is not a business development position. You won’t be expected to bring in work, develop firm strategy, or spend your days networking.

**We want your talents focused on architecture.** You’ll design. You’ll draw. You’ll lead projects. You’ll coordinate consultants. You’ll review drawings. You’ll solve difficult details. And you’ll help establish the level of design and documentation quality that every CREATE project should meet.

**WHAT YOU’LL DO**

· Design + Draw (Revit specifically)

· You will remain actively involved in the work.

· We want someone who can take an early idea and develop it into mature, thoughtful architecture, not simply manage the people doing it.

· You’ll work directly in projects, developing concepts, plans, elevations, materials, details and architectural solutions alongside our team.

· We’re looking for someone with a strong design eye who understands proportion, materiality, constructability and the details that make a building feel intentional.

· Lead Projects from Start to Finish

· You’ll provide senior architectural leadership throughout the entire life of a project, from early concepts through construction.

**That includes:**

· Concept and schematic design

· Design development

· Construction documentation

· Code and technical review

· Consultant coordination

· Permitting and bidding

· Construction administration

· Resolving complex design and construction conditions

**Our work includes multifamily, commercial, mixed-use, residential and other project types, with a significant emphasis on multifamily and commercial architecture.**

**Own Design + Drawing Quality**

One of the most important parts of this position is helping define and maintain the standard for CREATE’s architectural work.

You’ll lead our QA/QC process and review projects before major submissions and issuances.

We want you looking at both the big picture and the tiny stuff:

Does the building feel resolved? Are the plans actually working? Do the elevations have the right proportions? Are the details constructible? Are consultants coordinated? Does the drawing set communicate clearly? Would we be proud to put CREATE’s name on it?

You’ll have the authority and responsibility to push projects another round when they aren’t there yet.

**Build the CREATE Standard**

**CREATE is still a young firm, which means you won’t be inheriting 30 years of rigid standards. You’ll help us build them.**

**That may include improving:**

* Architectural detailing standards
* Revit and documentation standards
* Typical assemblies
* Drawing organization
* QA/QC processes
* Design review processes
* Consultant coordination
* Code review
* Specifications
* Constructability review
* Internal design critiques

*The goal isn’t to create bureaucracy. The goal is to make really good architecture consistently.*

**Teach + Mentor**

· We have a growing team of architects and designers, and we want someone who enjoys making the people around them better.

· Sometimes that means redlining a drawing.

· Sometimes it means sitting next to someone in Revit and working through a detail.

· Sometimes it means asking, “Why are we doing it that way?”

· We want someone who teaches through the work—not someone who simply reviews it from across the room.

**WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR**

**Our ideal candidate has:**

* 15+ years of professional architecture experience
* Active architectural licensure
* Significant experience with multifamily and commercial projects
* Strong design portfolio demonstrating mature, thoughtful architecture
* Extensive experience developing construction documents
* Strong Revit proficiency
* Excellent understanding of building assemblies and detailing
* Strong knowledge of building codes
* Experience coordinating structural, mechanical, electrical and civil consultants
* Experience taking projects through construction
* Strong QA/QC instincts
* Ability to identify problems before they become construction problems
* Ability to lead while remaining actively involved in production

**Just as importantly, we’re looking for someone who is:**

· Detail-oriented. Curious. Collaborative. Practical. Confident enough to challenge an idea. Humble enough to listen to another one.

· We don't need perfection or ego.

· We need someone who genuinely cares about getting the architecture right.

**WHERE YOU FIT AT CREATE**

This position works closely with CREATE’s leadership while having a very specific focus: the architecture itself.

Firm vision, business development and growth strategy will remain with Aspen and the ownership team. Operations, staffing and project delivery will continue to be led by Justin, Director of Operations.

Your lane will be architectural excellence: design quality, technical quality, project leadership, documentation and mentorship.

You will have significant influence over how CREATE designs buildings and how we document them, without the expectation that you spend your time selling work or running the business.

**WHY CREATE?**

We’re a small, growing architecture and development firm based in Sioux Falls.

That means this position is different from becoming another senior architect inside a large organization.

You’ll have the opportunity to help shape a practice.

You’ll work directly with the people making decisions. You’ll have meaningful influence over our projects and processes. You’ll be able to design, draw and solve problems instead of moving entirely into management.

**And you’ll help us answer an important question as CREATE grows:**

What should people expect when they see CREATE on a set of drawings or on the side of a building?

We want the answer to be: thoughtful design, technically strong architecture and work we're proud to put our name on.

If that sounds like the kind of responsibility you’ve been looking for, we’d love to talk.

Pay: $99,000.00 - $115,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Relocation assistance
* Vision insurance

Experience:

* Architectural Design : 10 years (Preferred)

License/Certification:

* Architecture License (Required)

Work Location: In person

card.description:
**Executive Director / VP of Quality**

I’m partnering exclusively with a growing Pharmaceutical Company looking to bring on a Vice President of Quality to lead its entire site Quality organisation, reporting directly to the CEO.

This is a senior, high-impact leadership opportunity for an established Quality executive to shape the site's Quality strategy, strengthen regulatory compliance and build a scalable Quality organisation as the business enters its next phase of growth and investment.

The successful individual will have oversight of both Quality Assurance and Quality Control, with significant influence across manufacturing operations, regulatory affairs, product development and wider business strategy. This is an opportunity to take genuine ownership of the Quality function, work closely with executive leadership and help drive the business forward while maintaining the highest standards of product quality and patient safety.

**Key areas of responsibility:**

* Set the overall Quality vision, objectives and priorities for the site, leading both QA and QC and ensuring the function supports business growth, operational performance and regulatory compliance.
* Act as the senior Quality representative to the FDA, leading inspections, maintaining inspection readiness, managing regulatory responses and overseeing sustainable remediation where required.
* Own the effectiveness and continuous improvement of the site QMS, ensuring systems remain robust, risk-based and aligned with evolving regulatory expectations.
* Provide executive oversight of batch release, deviations, investigations, CAPAs, change control, complaints, supplier quality, document control and data integrity, maintaining appropriate independent Quality decision-making.
* Oversee analytical and microbiological testing, OOS investigations, stability programmes, laboratory systems, environmental monitoring and associated compliance requirements.
* Partner with Manufacturing, Operations, Regulatory Affairs, R&D and Engineering to provide Quality oversight across product development, technology transfer, validation, commercial manufacturing and post-market activities.
* Establish meaningful Quality metrics, lead management reviews and use trend analysis, root-cause investigations and risk-based decision-making to address systemic issues and improve site performance.
* Build, lead and develop a high-performing Quality organisation, establishing the appropriate structure, technical capabilities, succession planning and resources to support the site's future needs.
* Work directly with the CEO and wider leadership team, translating complex regulatory requirements and Quality risks into practical business decisions while protecting compliance and patient safety.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* 12+ years of progressive experience within pharmaceutical manufacturing, with substantial Quality leadership experience in sterile pharmaceutical products.
* Proven executive-level leadership across multidisciplinary Quality organisations, ideally with responsibility for both QA and QC.
* A strong track record of leading FDA inspections, managing regulatory interactions and driving successful inspection readiness and remediation programmes.
* In-depth knowledge of US pharmaceutical cGMP requirements, particularly 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, with familiarity with relevant medical device regulations.
* Broad expertise across QMS, CAPA, validation and qualification, laboratory operations, supplier quality, complaints, risk management and data integrity.
* Experience supporting products throughout the lifecycle, from development and regulatory submissions through commercial manufacturing, release and post-market activities.
* Demonstrated success building Quality teams, developing future leaders and embedding a culture of accountability, compliance and continuous improvement.
* The ability to operate as a strategic business partner to executive leadership while maintaining the independence and authority required of the Quality function.
* A degree in a relevant scientific or technical discipline is required.

Apply today to learn more or reach out directly with your CV to rbanton@barringtonjames.com
